newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates ease in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates ease in slow trade.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates eased further on Wednesday in line with market expectations after the recent central bank's reserve requirement cut, which freed more funds in the banking system.
"Trade has been really slow today due to weak demand as the banks' accounts were mostly full," one dealer said.
Fresh morning trade was put at just 14.6 million kuna, with some 65 million kuna of both call money and term funds left on the supply side.
But one borrower was left empty handed, as there were not enough 60-day funds on offer.
The banking sector repaid some of the outstanding Lombard loans to the central bank with the morning total falling to 135 million kuna, a bank official said.

Call money loans, accounting for more than half of the money market trade, were made at lower 10 and 8.0 percent rates, the latter granted by foreign bank lenders. The price had been 10.5 percent so far.
Interbank term rates also edged down. One-month kuna funds were lent at 14.5 percent, down 50 basis points, and two-month at 16 and 17 percent -- one to two percentage points lower than before.
Tuesday's overnight trade totalled 10.2 million kuna with only one bank borrowing money to cover its shortfall. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
